intent.statement: A macOS user can install and launch Disk Steward as a polished native menu-bar application, understand its status at a glance, and receive a verifiably signed and notarized direct-distribution artifact without weakening the existing monitoring, evidence, privacy, or MCP behavior.

success_evidence.description: A stable Xcode project builds and archives a real Disk Steward .app with permanent product identity, a visible menu-bar item, bundled resources, and the read-only MCP helper included in the product.
The menu-bar dashboard presents capacity, growth, monitoring health, recency, and the evidence action in a compact Apple-like hierarchy that can be understood at a glance.
The status board remains clear and operable in light and dark appearance and in active, paused, degraded, no-baseline, and error states, with meaningful accessibility labels and keyboard behavior.

Existing whole-volume monitoring, watched-root evidence, export, read-only MCP, bounded retention, privacy exclusions, attribution honesty, and unprivileged fallback behavior continue to pass regression checks.

The release workflow produces a Developer ID-signed, hardened-runtime, notarized, stapled direct-distribution artifact when the required Apple credential is available, and otherwise fails closed with an exact human action instead of claiming release readiness.
Reproducible checks verify build, archive contents, nested-code signatures, entitlements, Gatekeeper assessment, launch behavior, tests, and absence of committed credentials or secrets.

The user can turn local MCP agent access on or off from the app; off stops and removes the private IPC endpoint, refuses agent queries with honest guidance, persists across launches, and does not pause monitoring or delete evidence.

Evidence follows a visible bounded lifecycle: recent exact detail becomes longer-lived summaries, snapshots are downsampled, anomalies have a finite detail window, database pressure produces explicit loss records, manual exports remain user-owned, and humans and agents can inspect the actual retained time ranges and storage usage.

A persistent evidence chain distinguishes current presence from historical activity and correctly reconciles baseline, create, modify, truncate, rename, replace, delete, scope change, restart, partial scan, and path reuse; cleanup and task-impact queries never treat deleted, unknown, or out-of-scope objects as current consumers.

constraints: Keep the product native Swift, AppKit, and SwiftUI on macOS 13 or newer, and preserve the existing Swift package as the reusable implementation boundary.

Use Apple Developer Team G3P6TU385Y with proposed identifiers com.marudankiji.disksteward, com.marudankiji.disksteward.endpoint, and group.com.marudankiji.disksteward; validate availability before registration.
Target direct distribution outside the Mac App Store with Developer ID, hardened runtime, secure timestamping, notarization, and stapling.

The standard app must build, launch, monitor, export, and serve read-only MCP without the restricted Endpoint Security entitlement; keep the optional system extension as a separately gated product path.
Do not store Apple credentials, private keys, account passwords, notarization profiles, or other secrets in the repository.
The user owns the final Xcode Signing & Capabilities selection and Organizer archive, distribution, and notarization interaction; automation must remain credential-free and inspectable.
Use system typography, semantic colors, materials, symbols, spacing, and native controls; avoid ornamental chrome that competes with storage health.

Treat MCP availability as a local privacy boundary: fresh installs default agent access off, the setting is explicit and persistent, disabling it closes the Unix socket promptly, and monitoring plus human evidence export remain independent.
Keep the evidence database bounded by both time and bytes; compaction may reduce precision but must never silently erase the fact that coverage was reduced.
Never automatically delete a human-created evidence export; report app-owned export count and size and leave deletion to an explicit user action.
Model paths as time-bounded bindings to file objects when stable filesystem identity is available; never equate path reuse with the same object without evidence.

Absence proves deletion only within a complete observation of an unchanged scope; failed, partial, capped, excluded, or changed-scope observations must produce unknown or out-of-scope state and coverage evidence instead.
non_goals: Submitting Disk Steward to the Mac App Store.
Automatically creating, revoking, exporting, or installing Apple signing certificates or private keys.
Making Endpoint Security approval or system-extension activation a prerequisite for the normal menu-bar app.
Adding cleanup, deletion, cache-purging, or other destructive disk tools.
Redesigning unrelated settings or evidence formats unless required for consistency with the new status board and bundle.
Adding cloud accounts, telemetry, an externally reachable service, or credential storage.

evidence.claim: The repository currently has a Swift package executable but no Xcode project or canonical application bundle target.
evidence.source: Repository inspection: Package.swift and absence of *.xcodeproj

evidence.claim: The current status popover gives explanatory copy and controls similar visual weight, weakening at-a-glance hierarchy in the user-provided screenshot.
The implemented monitoring, evidence, export, MCP, fallback, and privacy paths previously passed 105 automated tests.
evidence.source: Completed PLAN-DISK-STEWARD-001 evidence and swift test output
evidence.freshness: Verified in the immediately preceding implementation cycle

evidence.claim: Signing configuration contains placeholder team data and inconsistent dev.disksteward, group.dev.disksteward.shared, and group.com.disksteward.shared identifiers.
The machine has an Apple Distribution identity for Team G3P6TU385Y and Apple Development identities for a different team, but no verified Developer ID Application identity was observed.
evidence.source: security find-identity -v -p codesigning output supplied and inspected during this session

evidence.claim: Apple direct distribution requires Developer ID signing and notarization, with hardened runtime expected for notarized macOS software.
evidence.source: Apple Developer Documentation: Distributing outside the Mac App Store and Notarizing macOS software

evidence.claim: Apple guidance treats a popover as a focused surface for a small amount of related information and favors clear hierarchy, grouping, alignment, native controls, and concise labels.
evidence.source: Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Popovers, Layout, Buttons, and Design principles

evidence.claim: A temporary ad hoc application wrapper launched the existing executable and displayed the menu-bar popover, proving that the implementation can run in an application bundle while also demonstrating the need for a canonical bundle product.
evidence.source: Session launch and visual inspection of /tmp/DiskStewardDev.app

evidence.claim: The application currently starts its private Unix-socket evidence server unconditionally during StatusItemController initialization and stops it only when the controller is deinitialized.

The implemented default database lifecycle appends samples and events, runs retention on the first successful sample and then at most every six hours, converts eligible raw detail older than 7 days to hourly rows, converts hourly rows older than 30 days to daily rows, deletes daily rows older than 365 days, and enforces a 512 MiB ceiling through batch eviction and VACUUM.

Stored snapshots currently have no age-based compaction, unreviewed anomalies have no usable review transition and can remain until forced eviction, forced cap eviction prioritizes whole tables rather than a documented global evidence policy, and manual exports have no inventory or lifecycle UI.
evidence.source: EvidenceStore retention and eviction code, is_reviewed usage search, StatusBoardViewModel export path, and MonitoringSettingsView inspection

evidence.claim: The current local store occupies about 276 KiB with 14 snapshots and no raw events, while the user-owned export folder contains one approximately 12 KiB export.
evidence.source: Read-only du, file metadata, and sqlite3 queries against the current Disk Steward application-support and export directories

evidence.claim: Current storage events form historical deltas but there is no persistent current-file projection, so find_cleanup_candidates can return an old positive event after that path was deleted and get_provenance cannot authoritatively report present versus deleted state.
evidence.source: EvidenceStore schema plus AppEvidenceQueryBackend find_cleanup_candidates and get_provenance implementations

evidence.claim: Current reconciliation uses path-keyed in-memory metadata snapshots; missing entries become delete events even when a root is unavailable or a scan is capped, scope changes can appear as mass create or delete, restart loses the comparison baseline, and rename hints are discarded before reconciliation.
evidence.source: DirectoryMetadataScanner, PersistentMonitoringProbe, MonitoringLifecycleController, and TargetedFSEventsCollector integration inspection

evidence.claim: Provenance types exist but the running app does not connect FSEvents hints or privileged observations to persisted events; exported records synthesize method from confidence while actor and session fields are empty, and agent-session registrations are in memory only.
evidence.source: ProvenanceEngine usage search, PersistentMonitoringProbe, EvidenceBundleExporter, AppEvidenceQueryBackend, and AgentSessionRegistry inspection

evidence.claim: Several MCP queries export an arbitrary bounded event set before applying path or cleanup filters, default to basename shaping before provenance matching, and cannot query ended sessions, so filtering, truncation, identity, and historical task-impact semantics are not reliable at scale.
evidence.source: AppEvidenceQueryBackend broadRange, inlineBundle, get_provenance, find_cleanup_candidates, and get_task_impact inspection

decisions.question: How should the work become demonstrable before release signing is complete?
decisions.choice: Deliver a canonical launchable Xcode app and redesigned dashboard as the first increment, then add the direct-distribution pipeline as a cumulative second increment.
alternatives: Treat UI, packaging, and notarization as one all-or-nothing release increment
Polish only the SwiftPM executable without adding an Xcode application product
decisions.rationale: The first increment is independently useful and reviewable in Xcode, while Apple credential availability remains an external release dependency.

decisions.question: Which distribution channel and identity should define the release contract?
decisions.choice: Use direct distribution outside the Mac App Store under Team G3P6TU385Y with the proposed com.marudankiji.disksteward product identity.
alternatives: Mac App Store distribution
Keep temporary dev.disksteward identifiers
Ship unsigned or ad hoc signed builds
decisions.rationale: It matches the user's requested distributable desktop utility and Apple's Developer ID and notarization path; permanent identifiers also remove current configuration inconsistency.

decisions.question: Should Endpoint Security be embedded in the default release target now?
decisions.choice: Keep the standard app complete without Endpoint Security and retain the optional extension as a separately gated target until Apple grants the restricted entitlement.
alternatives: Block the application build on the extension
Remove the existing extension implementation
decisions.rationale: This preserves the product's proven fallback while avoiding a distribution blocker and retaining the future exact-provenance path.

decisions.question: What should dominate the status-board hierarchy?
decisions.choice: Lead with current free-space health and a concise growth assessment, then show monitoring state and recency, with evidence export as the single clear action.
alternatives: Keep all current labels and controls equally prominent
Show raw file records directly in the popover
Use a custom ornamental dashboard
decisions.rationale: This aligns the small popover with the user's immediate decision while detailed evidence remains available through export and MCP.

decisions.question: What should an MCP on or off control govern?
decisions.choice: Use one persistent Agent Access state, default off on fresh installs, that starts or stops the private local IPC service; show the state with a native toggle while keeping monitoring and manual evidence export independent.
alternatives: Only hide MCP UI while leaving the socket active
Edit Codex and Claude configuration files whenever the switch changes
Tie MCP availability to the monitoring pause control
decisions.rationale: A privacy control must enforce service availability rather than merely change presentation, and it should not mutate external client configuration or interrupt the app's core evidence collection.

decisions.question: How should evidence remain useful without becoming another disk consumer?
decisions.choice: Use a visible rolling lifecycle: 7 days of raw detail, 30 days of hourly path and capacity summaries, 365 days of daily summaries, finite anomaly detail, deterministic oldest-first pressure compaction, and a 512 MiB default hard ceiling; preserve manual exports as user-owned files and expose lifecycle status through UI and a read-only MCP tool.
alternatives: Keep all detailed evidence indefinitely
Replace the database with only the newest sample
Silently delete all app-created exports
Rely only on a byte ceiling without time windows or coverage reporting
decisions.rationale: The tiers preserve recent forensic detail and long-term growth trends, while explicit coverage and pressure records prevent an agent from mistaking compacted history for complete history.

decisions.question: How should Disk Steward distinguish files that exist now from files that only existed historically?
decisions.choice: Persist immutable observation runs and state observations, reconcile them through stable file objects and time-bounded path bindings, atomically maintain a current-file projection, and attach provenance, session context, rollups, retention, exports, and coverage gaps as separate linked records.
alternatives: Infer current existence by summing historical path deltas
Check file existence only when returning a query
Treat each path as one permanent object
Store only periodic full snapshots without an event chain
decisions.rationale: An event chain supplies history, the materialized projection answers current state, stable identity handles rename and path reuse, and explicit observation coverage prevents unavailable roots or capped scans from fabricating deletions.

nodes.title: Add enforceable MCP Agent Access control
nodes.summary: Introduce one persistent native on or off control that governs the private evidence IPC service and makes disabled access explicit without affecting monitoring or stored evidence.

acceptance_criteria.description: A fresh install defaults Agent Access off; the user can enable or disable it with a native toggle, and the choice persists across app relaunches.

Enabling Agent Access starts the owner-only Unix socket and permits the existing read-only MCP queries; disabling it closes active service availability, removes the socket, and causes the helper to return clear disabled-by-user guidance.
Changing Agent Access never pauses monitoring, deletes or rewrites evidence, modifies Codex or Claude configuration, expands MCP beyond read-only tools, or opens a network listener.
The control exposes on, off, starting, and degraded states without relying on color alone and remains synchronized anywhere its status is presented.

required_evidence.description: Fresh-install default, persistence, service start and stop, socket removal, disabled helper response, active query, monitoring independence, and accessibility state results.

deliverables: Native MCP access toggle and status
non_goals: Editing external Codex or Claude configuration on toggle
Pausing monitoring
Deleting evidence
Adding write-capable MCP tools or TCP access

nodes.title: Define the evidence identity, reconciliation, query, and lifecycle contract
nodes.summary: Specify one auditable model for what exists now, what changed historically, how strongly an actor is known, which intervals are covered, and how every evidence object is retained or retired.

acceptance_criteria.description: The contract defines ScopeVersion, ObservationRun, FileObject, PathBinding, FileStateObservation, CurrentFileState, ChangeEvent, ProvenanceClaim, AgentSession, CoverageGap, RollupBucket, RetentionRun, ExportRecord, and MCPAccessState with stable identifiers, timestamps, relationships, terminal states, and retention rules.

It separates immutable historical evidence from an atomically updated current-state projection, treats a first complete scan as baseline rather than creation, and defines create, modify, truncate, rename, replace, delete, path reuse, scope change, restart reconciliation, and out-of-scope transitions.

Absence proves deletion only after a complete observation of the same root and scope; unavailable, failed, permission-denied, depth-capped, entry-capped, or otherwise partial observations preserve prior state as unknown or stale and create a CoverageGap instead of deletion.

Every answer declares observation time, possible occurrence interval, scope and coverage, identity strength, provenance method and confidence, retained precision, truncation and pagination state, and known APFS reclaimability limitations.

The contract specifies atomic transaction boundaries, crash recovery, schema migration and replay invariants so compaction, restart, duplicate delivery, or partial failure cannot resurrect deleted objects or leave history inconsistent with current state.

The A/B/C fixture is normative: a complete baseline records A, B, and C as present; a later complete scan missing B records B deleted and current state A and C; the same missing observation under partial coverage records B unknown, not deleted.

required_evidence.description: Versioned schemas, state-transition tables, transaction invariants, lifecycle matrix, MCP result semantics, privacy rules, and adversarial scenario fixtures reviewed against the existing implementation.

non_goals: Implementing the schema
Claiming exact event time from periodic scans
Claiming an actor without direct or bounded attribution evidence
Adding destructive MCP operations

nodes.title: Persist observations and reconcile current file state safely
nodes.summary: Implement the durable identity and reconciliation core that can answer what is present now without confusing missing coverage, scope changes, renames, replacements, or restarts with deletion.

acceptance_criteria.description: Database migrations persist scope versions, observation runs and per-root completeness, stable file identity when available, temporal path bindings, state observations, current state, change events, and coverage gaps without discarding existing evidence.

One transaction commits an observation, its derived events, path-binding changes, current-state changes, and coverage result; retries are idempotent and recovery cannot expose half-applied observations.

Complete same-scope observations reconcile baseline, create, modify, truncate, rename, replace, delete, and path reuse, while partial or unavailable roots produce unknown or stale state and scope removal produces out-of-scope state.
Restart loads the last committed state and records offline or unreconciled coverage intervals; it never treats the first post-restart scan as proof that all intervening changes occurred at startup.
The normative A/B/C scenario returns only A and C as current after a complete deletion scan, retains B as a tombstoned historical object, and never emits B deleted after a partial scan.

required_evidence.description: Migration, transaction-failure, retry, restart, complete and partial coverage, scope change, A/B/C deletion, rename, replace, path reuse, hard-link or clone disclosure, and current-projection consistency fixtures.

non_goals: Guessing exact deletion time
Treating path as permanent identity
Deleting user files
Silently discarding partial-scan evidence

nodes.title: Persist provenance and agent-session evidence
nodes.summary: Connect filesystem and optional privileged observations to durable, confidence-labeled provenance claims and retained agent-session context without overstating who changed a file.

acceptance_criteria.description: FSEvents hints retain event identifiers, flags and rename or gap signals and are linked to observation runs; Endpoint Security observations, when available, remain a distinct stronger source rather than being synthesized from confidence.

Provenance claims persist method, actor when observed, process ancestry when observed, session link when supported, confidence, basis, time interval, contradictions, and supersession; unknown remains an explicit valid result.

Agent sessions persist start, heartbeat, end or expiry, workspace and task context across app restart, and historical task-impact queries can use ended retained sessions while clearly labeling temporal or workspace inference.

Rename, delete, path reuse, overlapping sessions, missing privileged access, dropped FSEvents and offline intervals preserve an ordered and uncertainty-aware chain without assigning unsupported authorship.

required_evidence.description: Fixtures for exact privileged events, FSEvents-only inference, unknown actor, rename and path reuse, session restart and expiry, overlapping sessions, dropped events, and export field fidelity.

non_goals: Requiring Endpoint Security for the standard app
Equating an active session with an observed writer
Fabricating exact actors or occurrence times

nodes.title: Implement bounded retention, coverage, and export lifecycle
nodes.summary: Keep current truth durable while compacting historical precision predictably, recording coverage loss, and separating temporary exports from user-owned evidence bundles.

acceptance_criteria.description: The default lifecycle keeps 7 days of raw event, state and provenance detail, at most 30 days of anomaly detail, 30 days of hourly summaries, and 365 days of daily summaries, with deterministic snapshot downsampling.

Current in-scope state remains available independently of historical-detail retention, tombstones remain only as long as required by the declared history window, and compaction cannot recreate a deleted object or erase an active object.

Retention runs at startup, at least every six hours while active, and near the 512 MiB default ceiling; pressure first compacts eligible detail, then evicts globally oldest history while persisting a RetentionRun and CoverageGap for forced loss.

MCP inline export temporaries are destroyed after each response; manual exports remain user-owned and are never automatically deleted, while ExportRecords report bounded inventory, hash, time range, precision, path-detail policy, and creation status.

Lifecycle status reports requested versus actually retained intervals, oldest and newest timestamps and counts per tier, database bytes versus cap, last compaction, forced evictions, current-state size, export inventory, and known gaps.

required_evidence.description: Boundary fixtures for every tier and snapshot rule, current-state survival, tombstone expiry, near-cap and over-cap behavior, persisted loss diagnostics, restart scheduling, and manual versus temporary exports.

non_goals: Automatically deleting manual exports
Evicting live current-state truth before compactable history
Claiming compacted history remains exact

nodes.title: Rebuild MCP queries on authoritative read models
nodes.summary: Expose current state, ordered evidence chains, lifecycle coverage, and task impact directly from indexed read models so bounded exports no longer distort query truth.

acceptance_criteria.description: Read-only tools provide live and persisted storage times, evidence lifecycle, paginated current consumers, growth, shrink and churn, ordered provenance, active and ended agent-session impact, revalidated cleanup candidates, and a complete bounded export.

Queries filter and order inside the evidence store before applying limits, match canonical identity before privacy path shaping, and report matched, returned, truncated, next cursor, requested versus retained interval, precision and coverage gaps.

find_cleanup_candidates reads only revalidated present current state and excludes deleted, unknown, stale, inaccessible, out-of-scope and path-reused objects; get_task_impact distinguishes historical bytes from surviving current bytes.

get_provenance returns the current object state followed by its ordered observation, change, provenance, session and coverage chain, preserving unknown actor and time intervals rather than synthesizing method or occurrence time.
list_active_writers is replaced by or retained only as a compatibility alias for list_active_agent_sessions, whose result explicitly does not claim observed writer identity.

required_evidence.description: Large-dataset filter-before-limit, duplicate basename, cursor stability, truncation, deleted and partial-state exclusion, ended-session impact, surviving bytes, retained-window gaps, privacy shaping, disabled Agent Access, and export parity fixtures.

deliverables: Corrected growth, provenance, task-impact and cleanup semantics
non_goals: Write-capable or cleanup MCP tools
Opening a network listener
Editing external client configuration
Treating registered sessions as observed writers

nodes.title: Redesign the menu-bar status board
nodes.summary: Replace the flat information stack with a compact native hierarchy centered on free-space health, recent growth, monitoring state, and one evidence action.

acceptance_criteria.description: The popover uses system materials, typography, semantic color, symbols, spacing, and controls to make capacity health and growth assessment the first readable layer without crowding.
Active, paused, degraded, no-baseline, and error states have concise non-conflicting copy, deterministic actions, appropriate focus order, and VoiceOver labels that do not rely on color alone.
Light and dark appearance previews and representative narrow-content checks reveal no clipping, ambiguous units, or inaccessible contrast.
Agent Access appears as a concise native privacy control with clear current state and does not visually compete with capacity health or conflate access with monitoring status.
The board shows last evidence freshness and database usage versus its cap concisely, with full retained-window and export-inventory detail available in Settings rather than crowding the popover.

required_evidence.description: State-matrix unit tests, accessibility inspection, light and dark screenshots, launch smoke evidence, and export-action verification.

required_context: TASK-230 Agent Access contract and state
deliverables: Concise evidence freshness and capacity status
non_goals: Displaying raw file logs in the popover
Changing the evidence schema
Adding destructive actions

nodes.title: Audit the polished native application increment
nodes.summary: Verify the canonical bundle, redesigned dashboard, embedded MCP helper, inherited evidence journey, and visual and accessibility states as one launchable product.

acceptance_criteria.description: A clean Xcode build launches the real app, exposes the menu item and redesigned popover, exports evidence, and serves a read-only MCP query from its bundled helper.
Representative capacity, growth, active, paused, degraded, no-baseline, and error states pass visual, accessibility, and interaction inspection in light and dark appearance.
All inherited Swift tests and privacy, fallback, retention, export, and MCP scenarios pass with no newly introduced destructive or network surface.
The fresh-install Agent Access default is off; enabling permits read-only MCP, disabling promptly refuses it, and both transitions leave monitoring and evidence intact.

Time-tier boundaries, snapshot downsampling, finite anomaly detail, pressure eviction, coverage-loss reporting, lifecycle UI, export ownership, and get_evidence_lifecycle compose without exceeding the configured database limit.

The complete evidence-chain matrix passes: A/B/C complete deletion versus partial uncertainty, restart gap, scope change, rename, replace, path reuse, current-only cleanup candidates, ended-session impact, ordered provenance, filter-before-limit pagination, and current-state survival through compaction.

required_evidence.description: Build and launch transcript, app-bundle inspection, UI screenshots and accessibility notes, MCP and export smoke results, full regression output, and changed-surface inspection.

non_goals: Changing product requirements to make a failure pass
Release notarization
Product implementation outside audit fixtures

nodes.title: Build the credential-free release and notarization handoff
nodes.summary: Provide inspectable archive, export, verification, and Xcode Organizer instructions that use Developer ID correctly while leaving account-backed final actions to the user.

acceptance_criteria.description: A release scheme archives the app with hardened runtime and production entitlements, and documented Xcode Organizer steps guide Developer ID distribution and notarization without embedding account credentials.

Release scripts accept an archive or exported artifact, verify expected identity class, nested MCP code, entitlements, timestamp, notarization and staple status, and Gatekeeper acceptance, and reject ad hoc or Apple Distribution-only output for direct release.
When Developer ID access is missing, the workflow stops with the precise Xcode or account-holder action and leaves a usable development build intact.

required_evidence.description: Archive logs, expected-failure fixtures, signed-artifact inspection when available, and a successful human handoff rehearsal.

non_goals: Saving notarization credentials
Automatically manipulating certificates
Requiring Endpoint Security for the standard release

nodes.title: Enforce distributable-artifact integrity and secret safety
nodes.summary: Turn common macOS release failure modes into deterministic checks so an incomplete or incorrectly signed artifact cannot be mistaken for the distributable product.

acceptance_criteria.description: Automated fixtures fail for wrong bundle identifiers, placeholder team values, missing hardened runtime, overbroad entitlements, unsigned or incorrectly signed nested code, absent notarization or staple evidence, and committed credential patterns.
The verification path checks the actual exported artifact and does not treat a successful compile, archive, or shallow codesign command as distribution success.

required_evidence.description: Passing valid fixtures, rejecting invalid fixtures, repository secret scan, entitlement diff, and actual artifact inspection transcript.

required_context: Apple code signing and notarization requirements
non_goals: Weakening checks for locally available identities
Scanning user files outside the repository
Changing application features

nodes.title: Audit the direct-distribution release
nodes.summary: Verify the exact exported application and rerun the polished app journey before declaring it safe to share outside Xcode.

acceptance_criteria.description: The exact exported artifact has the canonical identifiers, Developer ID Application signatures for all executable code, hardened runtime, least-privilege production entitlements, successful notarization and stapling, and Gatekeeper acceptance.

The exported app launches on the target Mac, exposes the status board, preserves the fresh-install MCP-off default, successfully toggles read-only Agent Access on and off, records or reads a sample, exports evidence, reruns the inherited evidence-chain matrix including A/B/C deletion and partial-scan uncertainty, and keeps the full regression suite green.
If user-owned Apple credentials or approval are unavailable, the gate records a blocked release with exact remediation and does not mark OUTCOME-220 or INTENT-002 verified.

required_evidence.description: Artifact hash and contents, codesign and entitlement output, notarization and staple result, Gatekeeper result, launch and product-journey transcript, complete tests, and secret-safety result.

deliverables: Truthful pass or blocked release disposition
non_goals: Editing product code during the audit
Claiming notarization without Apple evidence
Changing acceptance criteria
